newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rothschild breaks ground with public results.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rothschild breaks ground with public results.

text.p: Merchant banking group Rothschild on Tuesday broke with a 200-year tradition and published its results for the first time, reporting a 66 percent rise in operating profits for the year.
Swiss-registered Rothschilds Continuation Holdings AG (RCH), parent of the N M Rothschild group, announced operating profits of 179 million Swiss francs ($122 million) for the year to March 31.
"On the whole, considering gyrations in the financial markets, we've done pretty well," Sir Evelyn de Rothschild, RCH chairman told Reuters.
Rothschild re-iterated the banking dynasty's determination to remain independent, stressing the opportunities this independence presented.
"I don't think there's any question of change of ownership. The independence of the Rothschild group is very important," he said.
"Those of us who are independent have got a greater opportunity than some of those that aren't independent and larger groupings," he added.

Rothschild said larger banks were going to face problems in the years ahead because they thought they could do everything. Rothschild would never get "big by numbers" but would produce good results with its specialist and advisory capacity.

The group said its traditional strengths in corporate banking and banking for mining and other natural resource companies had been evident in a range of deals in Australia, South Africa and North and South America over the period.
It said investment banking and private banking had performed particularly well, and its Asia Pacific and North American operations had performed strongly.
Total funds under management at Rothschild's asset management group, which was reorganised last year, grew to more than $30 billion, with a 20 percent increase in revenues in Britain.
A year after the group set up a joint venture with Dutch financial services group ABN AMRO, Rothschild said the partnership had been "a remarkable success story", opening new business opportunities.
He said the relationship with the ABN AMRO group was a long one and there had been no teething problems in the equity capital markets joint venture.
"We are open to any ideas on joint venturing, where it suits both parties," he said.
N M Rothschild, which will celebrate its 200th anniversary next year, also confirmed it had formed a global partnership of its main operating companies in Britain, Australia, Hong Kong and Singapore.
Called N M Rothschild & Sons Partnership, the structure is divided into three business divisions which will be managed and co-ordinated globally aimed at serving clients who operate around the world.
The three divisions are -- treasury and bullion trading, resource banking and investment banking.
This strategy brings together the group's capital, allowing Rothschilds to manage its resources more efficiently and competitively, it said.

"We like to think we can compete with the big boys," Rothschild said. But he does not believe in competing with the U.S. firms in their own backyard, although Rothschild does have a presence there to concentrate on its specialist expertise.
The partnership would mean the group had a fully integrated international balance sheet. This required investment in systems, but the group had not "gone over the top" on its spending, he added.

Group finance director Andrew Didham told Reuters a rise in administrative expenses to 616 million Swiss francs from 418 million Swiss francs was largely due to the depreciation of the currency and the fact that most of the group's personnel costs were elsewhere.
Rothschild also confirmed the establishment of a world-wide investment banking committee for the British arm of Rothschild and the French business run by another part of the family.
This committee is chaired by Evelyn's cousin Baron David de Rothschild. It will work much more closely and should lead to a much better marketing effort between the various areas, Rothschild said.
"The combination these days is getting across borders," he said. A recent example of this philosophy at work had been Rothschild's role in the privatisation of Deutsche Telekom AG .
And although some of its operations around the world were quite small, they were crucial to winning business because this network showed a commitment to the countries in which they were based.
"Competition is huge at the moment. Its a hard-fought battle to win but we've won quite a number of mandates so there must be something we are doing right," Rothschild said.

Asked why the group had chosen to make its results public for the first time, Rothschild said the group had been reorganised in order to make it compete and he wanted to prove that independent merchant banks "have a huge role to play in the international financial scene". ($ = 1.465 Swiss Francs)
